passage.title: GRANDPA'S SUNDAY LUNCH
passage.subtitle: A weekly family tradition in Cardiff
paragraphs: Every Sunday at midday, twelve members of the Davies family arrive at Grandpa Arthur's red-brick house in Cardiff. Arthur is seventy-four years old, and cooking Sunday lunch for his children and grandchildren is the highlight of his week.

Arthur always starts cooking at nine o'clock in the morning. He roasts beef or chicken in the oven, boils fresh carrots and peas from his garden, and makes a large bowl of warm gravy. Meanwhile, Grandma Megan bakes a sweet fruit crumble with apples or pears.

The dining room has got a huge oak table that Arthur built forty years ago. Before everyone sits down at one o'clock, the youngest grandchildren carefully set the table with white plates and colourful glasses. There is always plenty of talking, joking and sharing news from school and work.

When lunch finishes, nobody leaves immediately. The adults drink tea in the living room while the children play chess or draw pictures on the rug. Everyone agrees that Grandpa's house feels like the warmest place in the city.
